title: Iterative retrieval & sparse-KV experiment notes
content:
TL;DR:
Quick synthesis from reading and demos (Mar 22–31). Iterative/multi-pass retrieval seems promising for boosting recall on long contexts with modest model-size overhead,
but it complicates latency budgeting and KV-cache usefulness. Notes here are brainstorming + concrete micro-experiments we can run on Redwood Dedicated and a small Private cluster.

What I read / watched this week:
- Paper: Iterative Retrieval for Long Queries (notes + intuition) — key idea: retrieval + model feedback loop to add
  context incrementally rather than a single massive retrieval.
- Blog: engineering tradeoffs for multi-pass RAG (practical latency/cost breakdowns).
- Internal demo: prototype that stitches 2 retrieval passes with minibatching (Lina's PoC).

Key takeaways / heuristics:
1) Early stop on retrieval: if model confidence score > threshold after pass 1, skip pass 2. Saves ~40–60% of extra cost in PoC.
2) KV-cache interplay: when we append documents after generation, we break token alignment for cached prefixes —
   need to either (a) flush KV cache for that session, (b) build an append-aware cache that stores alternative prefix hashes, or
   (c) keep retrieved docs off-cache and only present as context input (worse latency).
3) Batching: multi-pass reduces effective batchability because second pass depends on first-pass outputs. Could mitigate by
   queuing second-pass requests in micro-batches with a short window (10–50 ms). Trade: latency jitter vs throughput.

Open questions (short):
- What confidence signal is cheap and reliable enough? Logit-normalization? Small auxiliary head?
- How frequently do we need to write to persistent KV store vs ephemeral in-memory for append operations?
- Can we do a cheap token-level sketch of retrieved docs to allow prefix-friendly caching?

Experiment backlog (prioritized):
A. Baseline instrumentation run (2 days):
   - Dataset: 5k customer-like queries (mix support dialogs, long docs).
   - Modes: single-pass RAG (top-k), iterative 2-pass with confidence gating, iterative 3-pass (aggressive).
   - Measure: p50/p95 latency, tokens/server-second, per-request cost estimate (tokens + retrieval cost), answer F1/ROUGE on labelled subset.
   - Where: Dedicated small cluster (g4-like equivalent), and Private (single-node).
B. KV-cache behavior matrix (1 week):
   - Variant 1: default KV cache + flush after retrieval append.
   - Variant 2: append-aware in-memory staging (no flush, but slower compose).
   - Variant 3: no KV caching for sessions using iterative retrieval (baseline).
   - Metrics: cold vs warm start latency, cache hit-rate, additional memory pressure, cost simulation.
C. Micro-batching second pass (1 week):
   - Implement a 20 ms staging window to aggregate second-pass inputs.
   - Test p95 impact and effective throughput. Track user-perceived tail latency.

Quick hacks / prototype notes (commands & pseudo):
- Local sim (toy): run 1000 queries through model-local + elasticsearch index. Script: tools/iter-retrieval/run_sim.py --mode 2pass --confidence-threshold 0.7 --batch-window-ms 20
- Instrumentation: add tags to traces: retr_pass=1/2, retr_count, retr_ms, kv_flush=true/false. Hook into console traces (per-route).
- Cost calc: tokens_cost = (generation_tokens * gen_unit_cost) + (retrieved_docs * retr_cost); normalize to cents per query.

Potential risks / mitigation:
- Risk: interactive apps (chat) will blow p95 when second pass triggers often. Mitigate with conservative gating and fallback to shorter retrievals.
- Risk: cache fragmentation if many append variants. Mitigation: limit iterative retrieval to sessions marked as "high-value" or heavy queries, not every request.

Ideas for Redwood-specific product hooks:
- Rollout knob in Console: iterativeRetrieval: off | conservative | aggressive (maps to thresholds + max passes). Expose expected cost uplift.
- Auto-suggest: Console Optimize should recommend iterative mode only when loss in single-pass recall > X and expected cost delta < Y.
- SLA note: document that iterated retrieval increases variance; expose p95 change before enabling.

Action items (mine / next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Spin up baseline runs A + B locally and in Dedicated, collect traces (due Apr 5).
- [ ] Prototype 20ms batch window for pass 2 (co-owner: Ishaan).
- [ ] Write short Confluence deck summarizing tradeoffs and a recommended default for Console (draft Apr 9).

Notes to self / scribbles:
- If we keep retrieved docs out of KV cache, we might do a hybrid: keep raw doc ids in cache and only fetch text when model asks (lazy fetch).
- Could try lightweight reranker (tiny transformer) to compute cheap confidence — might be cheaper than second-pass generation in many cases.

Random links I want to follow up:
- Retrieval + generation calibration paper (link above).
- Lina's PoC repo (GH link in linked_artifacts).

End. This is a working doc — will iterate.
